name: Oxiracetam
lead: Oxiracetam is a synthetic nootropic of the racetam family, related to piracetam. People take it for focus, memory and mental clarity, with the stated payoff that better concentration and recall help them keep up study, work and training routines, which in turn feed physique and presentation goals.[1]

It has been used as a prescription medicine for cognitive impairment in some countries, and it has been tested in randomized trials in vascular cognitive impairment, post-stroke cognitive decline and traumatic brain injury.[12][13][4] Laboratory work links racetams to cholinergic and glutamate (AMPA receptor) systems, though no single mechanism is agreed.[5][6]
Wikipedia describes oxiracetam as a very mild stimulant, prescription-only in Australia and unscheduled but not FDA-approved for any medical use in the US.[17]

quick.overview:
Oxiracetam is a racetam, a class of cognition-oriented compounds related to piracetam. It was developed in the 1970s-80s and has been marketed in some European and Asian countries for cognitive impairment.

In communities focused on self-improvement, it is used as a nootropic aimed at focus, memory and learning, supporting the study and work that sit behind a lot of ascension routines.
quick.mechanism: Racetams are reported to modulate AMPA-type glutamate receptors and cholinergic activity, and oxiracetam has been studied for effects on acetylcholine in animals. Reviews note that no commonly accepted single mechanism has been established.
quick.risks: Reviews of the piracetam-like nootropics describe very low toxicity and few serious side effects; headache is the effect most often mentioned. It is a prescription drug in some countries and is not approved by the US FDA.

paras: Oxiracetam has no direct effect on appearance that sources describe. Users describe it as a focus and memory aid that helps them keep up study, work and training.
It has been prescribed in some countries for cognitive impairment associated with degenerative or vascular dementia, and post-stroke recovery.[1][7]

Reviews of racetams report reversal of experimentally induced amnesia in animals, evidence of cholinergic interaction, and positive modulation of AMPA-sensitive glutamate receptors in neuronal cultures, with no single accepted mechanism.[5][6][8][9]

Animal work from the 1980s reported that oxiracetam prevented electroshock-induced fall in brain acetylcholine and amnesia in rodents,[18] and that nootropics reversed scopolamine-induced amnesia in mice.[19] A 1987 study examined interactions between oxiracetam, aniracetam and scopolamine on behavior and brain acetylcholine.[9] Wikipedia also cites a mouse study in which oxiracetam improved spatial learning in a water maze and correlated with increased membrane-bound protein kinase C.[17] A review of racetams (1965 to 1992, 407 references) found no affinity for a long list of receptors and noted increased turnover of several neurotransmitters.[5]

Wikipedia gives oral bioavailability of about 56 to 82 percent, peak serum levels one to three hours after oral intake and onset at 30 to 90 minutes, with an elimination half-life of roughly 8 hours in healthy people and 10 to 68 hours in renal impairment. About 84 percent is excreted unchanged in urine, and brain concentrations reach about 5.3 percent of blood levels.[17]

Wikipedia summarises dementia studies as mixed: mild-to-moderate dementia patients showed some gains on tests of logic, attention, memory and spatial orientation, results were inconsistent in Alzheimer patients, improvements were reported in post-concussion syndrome and other organic brain syndromes, and in mild-to-moderate traumatic brain injury it appeared ineffective for memory and cognition.[17] A double-blind randomized trial in organic brain syndrome and a controlled trial in Alzheimer disease were published in 1987 and 1992.[10][11] A 1989 Italian review describes oxiracetam trials in cognitive disorders.[7]

The more recent trials are in Asian multicenter settings. The phase IV trial in vascular cognitive impairment (protocol published 2023) planned 500 participants with cognitive complaints three months after stroke, randomized to oxiracetam or placebo for 36 weeks alongside an exercise protocol, with co-primary outcomes of change in the Mini-Mental State Examination and the Clinical Dementia Rating Sum of Boxes, wrist actigraphy and resting-state functional MRI.[12] A Korean multicenter placebo-controlled trial commissioned by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety examined oxiracetam for preventing post-stroke cognitive impairment and its interaction with physical activity using neuroimaging.[3][13]

In a multicentre double-blind trial of 590 adults with traumatic brain injury at 51 Chinese hospitals (2019 to 2024), participants were randomized 2:2:1 to L-oxiracetam, oxiracetam or placebo. On the Loewenstein Occupational Therapy Cognitive Assessment 90 days after treatment, least squares mean change was 20.45 for L-oxiracetam, 15.90 for oxiracetam and 11.47 for placebo; the difference between L-oxiracetam and placebo was 8.97 points (P < 0.001), and serious adverse events did not differ among groups.[4][14]

Oxiracetam appeared among 21 drugs in a network meta-analysis of 194 randomized trials in vascular dementia, in which butylphthalide, huperzine A, edaravone, rivastigmine and memantine ranked highest for MMSE scores.[15] A study at high altitude examined whether oxiracetam or fastigial nucleus stimulation reduced cognitive injury,[20] and a 2026 phase 1 registration studies IQ-test reliability under racetam-class compounds in healthy people.[16]
Reviews describe the piracetam-like nootropics as having very low toxicity and lacking serious side effects.[5]
Wikipedia says several studies suggest it is safe, even at high doses over long periods, without detailing specific side effects.[17]

On the T Nation forum, oxiracetam appears in threads on brain-function boosters and study aids, where members discuss racetams alongside vinpocetine, DMAE and aniracetam for class and exam periods and ask others for experience and sourcing.[21][22] These are individual reports and stacks assembled by members; the forum posts contain no controlled data.
Oxiracetam is Schedule 4 (prescription-only) in Australia and unscheduled in the US, where the FDA has not approved it for any medical use.[17]
